notes: DEGRADED TELEMETRY / TRACE SAMPLING (adversarial, first sample_traces scenario). Culprit is 'refactor(pipeline): per-record config resolution' (services/pipeline-transformer/transform.go, deployed to pipeline-transformer at 15:05): it moves the config lookup from once-per-batch (`cfg, err := s.config.Get(ctx, batch[0].Type)`, called before the loop) to once-per-record (`cfg, err := s.config.Get(ctx, rec.Type)`, called inside `for _, rec := range batch`) — a realistic change (it lets records within a batch carry different types) whose side effect is an N-fold multiplication of calls to config-svc, N being the batch size. The commit message and diff never mention this cost; it must be inferred from the code motion (the Get call crossing the loop boundary) plus derived telemetry. PROOF CHAIN: (1) config_svc_requests_per_s ramps 40 -> 3900 starting 15:15 (10 min after the 15:05 deploy, once traffic volume ramps through the new code path); (2) pipeline-transformer's own batch_process_p95_ms ramps in lockstep from 15:15 (180ms -> 2400ms) because each batch's total wall time is now dominated by N sequential config-svc round trips instead of one; (3) config-svc's own rpc_latency_p95_ms only starts climbing at 15:22, 7 minutes later (15ms -> 480ms) as sustained 3900 rps saturates it — config-svc is a downstream victim of the fanout, not the origin; (4) dashboard-svc's dashboard_data_lag_s (the alerting metric) ramps from 15:35 (5s -> 640s) as pipeline-transformer's collapsed throughput starves it of fresh data, crossing the 300s alert threshold by ~15:59 and firing at 16:10. BATCH-SIZE ARITHMETIC: pipeline-transformer's routine 'batch flushed' INFO log line carries a constant `records=96` field on every occurrence (pre- and post-onset alike — a stable batch-size fact, not an incident marker, and never quoted in the culprit diff). Pre-onset, config_svc_requests_per_s's baseline of ~40 IS the batches-processed-per-second rate (the old code issued exactly one config-svc call per batch, a 1:1 ratio). Post-onset, every one of the ~96 records in a batch now issues its own call, so the expected rate is batches-per-s x records-per-batch =~ 40 x 96 = 3840, which lines up with the observed ramp to ~3900 (the small gap is realistic jitter/rounding, not a contradiction) — this is the derivable arithmetic proof of the N+1 fanout, built entirely from two independent metrics plus one constant log field, never from a leaked diff constant. DEGRADATION MECHANICS: sample_traces keeps whole traces (never individual spans) with probability rate=0.01 via `md5(trace_id) % 10000 < rate*10000`; at rate=0.01 well over 99% of the auto-generated ProcessBatch trace_flow traffic (15/hour, ending at onset 15:15 per convention) is dropped, so traces.json is visibly sparse relative to the ~2.25h of pre-onset flow traffic and the incident's log volume — a solver should notice the tiny surviving span count and treat traces as corroborating color, not primary evidence. Two hand-authored exemplars were deliberately chosen with trace_ids verified (via md5(trace_id) % 10000 < 100) to survive this sampling: dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0103 (md5%10000=77) is a healthy PRE-onset exemplar at 14:30 (before the 15:05 deploy) showing the OLD shape — exactly one config-svc 'config.Get' child span per ProcessBatch span; dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0231 (md5%10000=68) is a POST-onset exemplar at 15:50 (mid-ramp) showing the NEW shape — the batch span erroring generically 'batch deadline exceeded' with exactly 3 generic 'config.Get' child spans, all at NORMAL durations (9-11ms, same ballpark as the healthy exemplar's 8ms). This is a deliberate design choice: the surviving post-onset trace proves the per-record call pattern now exists (multiple children instead of one) without directly exposing the full 96x multiplication a real batch would show — a solver who only reads traces would see '3 calls, all fast' and could wrongly conclude the fanout is mild. The real magnitude (40 -> 3900 rps, ~96x) only comes from config_svc_requests_per_s; this is the intended lesson of the sample_traces degradation — metric corroboration must replace trace-count evidence when traces are this sparse. first_failing_service is pipeline-transformer: it is both the culprit's deploy target and the first service whose own metric (batch_process_p95_ms) starts ramping, tied at 15:15 with config_svc_requests_per_s (a load figure imposed on config-svc by the caller, not config-svc's own degradation) — config-svc's own health metric (rpc_latency_p95_ms) only degrades 7 minutes later, confirming it is a downstream victim, not the origin. blast_radius = [config-svc, dashboard-svc] (config-svc is overwhelmed upstream load; dashboard-svc is the alerting victim). TRAP LOGIC: compression-decoy ('perf(config-svc): add response compression', config-svc, deployed 14:40, pre-onset) is the response-shaping trap: gzip-encoding the config payload changes response SIZE/bytes-on-wire, never request COUNT — it cannot multiply config_svc_requests_per_s, which is the discriminating metric. parallel-decoy ('feat(pipeline): parallel batch workers', pipeline-transformer, deployed 14:20, pre-onset) is the flag-gated trap: the new goroutine-per-batch path is wrapped in `if s.flags.Enabled("pipeline_parallel_batches")`, and flags.json shows this flag created OFF at 14:10 and never flipped for the rest of the window, so the new code path never executes regardless of deploy timing. metrics-helper-decoy ('refactor(pipeline): extract batch metrics helper', pipeline-transformer, deployed 15:10, only 5 minutes after the real culprit, to the SAME service) is the most dangerous decoy: right service, right neighborhood, right file family. It is exonerated purely by mechanism: the diff only extracts the existing `batchSizeHist.Observe`/`batchesFlushed.Inc()` body into a new `recordBatchMetrics` helper called from the unchanged `emitBatchFlushed` — a semantics-preserving refactor with zero control-flow change, touching neither the config lookup nor the per-record loop. banner-decoy ('refresh banner copy', dashboard-svc, deployed 16:05, 5 minutes before fired_at 16:10) is classic innocent-deploy-near-alert bait: a one-character copy change (added '!') in an unrelated file. Pre-onset invariant: both compression-decoy (14:40) and parallel-decoy (14:20) deploy before onset (15:15), alongside 18 deploys_auto entries (>=6 pre-onset, cyclic across all five services) that are pure background noise: routine dependency/docs/CI/test tweaks touching none of transform.go, workers.go, handler.go, or metrics.go. Patterns are victim-first: dashboard-svc's ERROR pattern (8/min from 15:40 -> ~1120 total) is the loudest, ahead of config-svc's WARN pattern (5/min from 15:20 -> ~800), ahead of pipeline-transformer's own WARN pattern (3/min from 15:15 -> ~495, the quietest despite being the true cause); 3 patterns_extra stale background negatives (kafka rebalancing on ingest-worker, disk usage on search-svc, TLS renewal on config-svc; counts 50-72, delta +2) sit below all three incident patterns as unrelated pre-existing chatter. A search-svc index_lag_ms spike (baseline ~90 -> 450, 13:20-13:50) self-heals nearly 90 minutes before onset and is unrelated red-herring noise on an uninvolved service. Remediation: roll back pipeline-transformer to before the per-record config-resolution change.
